title: Transwap Business Bank
intro: TranSwap is a fintech platform that helps businesses send and receive money globally. You can hold multiple currencies and make payments to over 100 countries easily.
body: TranSwap is a fintech firm that specialises in **cross-border payments, multi-currency accounts and global business banking services**.
It was founded in Singapore in 2015 and has since expanded globally, including into the UK.
In the UK it is registered as an electronic money institution under the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) — Firm Reference Number 963951.
Multi-currency account: You can hold and convert across multiple currencies (up to 34 in some cases) and receive or make payments globally.

Global collections & payments: If your business works internationally (e.g., you sell abroad, or pay suppliers overseas), TranSwap lets you collect locally (in GBP, USD, EUR etc) and send to over 100+ countries.
Transparent and lower FX / transfer costs: Their model emphasises fewer hidden fees and more favourable conversion/transfer rates for businesses operating across borders.
Digital-first, streamlined: The services are designed for online/app-based management — useful if you prefer handling things via your device rather than traditional branch banking.
**Why choose us (if you’re using our recommendation)?**
We think TranSwap is a strong option if your situation is something like:
You’re a freelancer, business or startup that operates in more than one country or currency.
You’re regularly receiving payments from overseas customers or paying overseas suppliers.
You want to simplify your money-management across borders (rather than juggling many bank accounts in many places).
You prefer modern, digital-friendly services and value transparency of fees and exchange rates.

TranSwap is not a traditional bank: it operates as an electronic money institution (EMI). That means different protections apply compared to full banks (e.g., deposit guarantee schemes may not cover funds in the same way).
Despite being regulated, any digital/fintech provider carries some risk (e.g., service changes, regulatory shifts, foreign-currency risks).

If your business is purely domestic (UK only, GBP only) and doesn’t deal with international payments or currencies, then a simpler local bank might suffice — the global features of TranSwap may be underused.
You should check the specific fees, terms, exchange rates, and how user-friendly the interface/support is for your needs.
